images.alt: Three revolver cartridges standing upright and lying flat: .32 S&W Long and .32 H&R Magnum with visible lead or jacketed bullet noses, and a 7.62x38R Nagant whose case mouth is crimped shut over a bullet seated entirely inside the case
images.caption: A commercial 7.62×38mmR round beside .32 S&W Long and .32 H&R Magnum for scale — the Nagant case shows no exposed bullet at all, because the bullet is seated flush with (and crimped inside) the case mouth.

images.alt: Seven brass 7.62×38mmR cases standing in a row, each showing a slightly different case-mouth crimp from a different commercial manufacturer
images.caption: Seven commercially manufactured 7.62mm Nagant cases (RWS and Geco of Germany, an unmarked GB headstamp, SFM of France, PS of Czechoslovakia, and a modern GFL of Italy), showing how the mouth crimp that seals the bullet inside the case varies by maker.
